note: The regression stratum: one named case per distinct property carried forward, with every source retained as provenance. A case states a falsifiable present-tense property verified through structural assertions and counters, never recorded-byte equality — recorded bytes pin rendering, and that is the coverage corpus's job, not this one's. Every case is dormant until the layer named by its `venue` lands, and binding it is a deliberate edit to this file that names the tests carrying it. A case with `mandatory` set is pinned in the harness as well, so removing it takes more than an edit here. See docs/decisions/0005-regression-stratum.md and docs/decisions/0009-regression-properties-not-recordings.md.

cases.name: a-measurement-lane-proves-it-measured
cases.property: A case's lane assignment is bound to the file it sits in, not to a set of sanctioned spellings, so a case renamed or re-laned fails the guard instead of being adopted by a lane nobody meant to run it. An ignore shape the guard cannot parse fails rather than passing through, and the guard fails when it checked nothing.

cases.name: a-measurement-step-asserts-a-nonzero-pass-count
cases.property: A step that selects its cases by kind rather than by name asserts a non-zero pass count, so a filter that matches nothing fails the step instead of reporting green having run nothing. A lane whose only evidence is that its runner exited zero has measured nothing and says so.

binding.reason: its carrier is a workflow script, and a test reference in this file is a workspace-relative source file and a `#[test]` function in it — a grammar that cannot name a CI step.

cases.name: budget-is-a-read-budget-not-a-recompute-budget
cases.property: A budget assertion is a derivation-counter ceiling on the warm path — documents hydrated, rules evaluated, statements executed — never a wall-clock ceiling. Where a clock is read at all, the asserted quantity is the machine-independent ratio of verb cost to a pinned refusal-stub round-trip floor, and a ratio never stands in for a counter.

binding.reason: there is no warm path to count and no floor verb to pin: the composition root is a stub, so no request surface exists to hold a budget.

cases.name: comment-claims-are-test-bound
cases.property: A comment asserting a cost shape — one SELECT, scoped, O(affected) — carries a counter assertion binding it in the same suite. An unbacked cost claim is a defect, because a violation narrated in the code that commits it reads as documentation.

binding.reason: no counter helper has a subject yet; the convention binds when the first cost-shaped comment lands beside a counter that can hold it. Cost-shaped comments do exist, in norn-text's frontmatter split and text derive, and what backs them is a wall-clock ratio in a soak lane rather than a counter — which is the evidence kind this case would hold them to. One more sits on the value model's by-key view, where the claim is which of two arms costs less at a given entry count: a structural case pins the count the arms turn at, so the constant cannot move unreviewed, but nothing counts the comparisons either arm makes.

cases.name: fixtures-carry-real-content-volume
cases.property: Every scale fixture declares document count and byte volume, and its body-length distribution is long-tailed rather than uniform. A tree at ~84 bytes per document understates a real collection's ~10 KB by about 120x, and perf and counter assertions taken against one are inadmissible.

cases.name: guard-binds-executed-sql
cases.property: Every plan-shape assertion is taken from SQL captured out of the executing request, never from a literal authored in the test. A test naming a query no request path issues fails as unbound rather than passing against a string nobody executes.

binding.reason: the harness pairs a plan with the statement it was taken of, but no builder emits SQL yet, so there is no request from which a statement could be captured.

cases.name: harness-assertions-observe-stable-facts
cases.property: A harness assertion names a fact the platform guarantees: it waits on an observable condition rather than on a sleep or a TTL boundary, and never asserts over an identifier the kernel may reuse — inode numbers are reused eagerly on ext4 and tmpfs, so inequality between them is not a fact about identity.

binding.reason: no suite waits on a background condition, because there is no daemon, watcher or idle reaper to observe.

cases.name: harness-processes-are-bounded-and-exec-safe
cases.property: A spawned child is bounded and its outcome is legible: output is captured up to a declared limit, an exit code and a terminating signal are reported apart, and a binary written and then executed runs from a path whose writer is closed, so an exec never races ETXTBSY.

cases.name: harness-runs-under-isolated-state-roots
cases.property: Every harness invocation runs under isolated cache and state homes supplied by a shared helper rather than by per-test discipline, and inherits nothing else: a run's environment is the allowlist, the path, and the lease root, every isolated variable points inside that run's own sandbox, two sandboxes share no directory, and a sandbox is gone when it drops. Per-test discipline in place of the shared helper is the shape this forbids: it is what leaves 27 test files one missing variable away from deleting a real operator's state. The lease root is the one variable a run does not get a private copy of, and it is forwarded as the parent's resolved value rather than derived again in the child: the isolation a sandbox gives is partitioning, and a run that partitioned the root of a cross-process exclusion would take every lease uncontended and report nothing about having done so.

cases.name: harness-self-check-is-not-immune-to-contamination
cases.property: A harness's own self-check is subject to the contamination it exists to detect. Traffic a harness generates is isolated from any resident service by construction, and a contaminated run fails the self-check rather than attributing divergence to the subject: one contaminated output region reads as 44 phantom drifts and 7x wall clock, and a self-check that stays green through it is the shape this forbids.

binding.reason: there is no resident service to contaminate and no comparison harness to check itself; the class binds with the first harness that generates its own traffic.

cases.name: harness-waits-have-deadlines
cases.property: A harness wait on a child carries a deadline: it either observes the child's end or kills the child, reaps it, and reports the timeout naming the bound it passed, so no run hangs until the runner's own timeout decides for it. A child that ends inside its bound reports what it did — the deadline observes, and never preempts.

cases.name: instrumentation-exists-and-is-consumed
cases.property: Every derivation counter and computed duration has at least one consumer — an assertion or an emitted record — and a metric computed and dropped fails the build. Counters are readable from the process harness without a debug build.

binding.reason: no counter has a producer yet; the rule binds when the substrate emits its first.

cases.name: mission-property-is-a-test
cases.property: Each sentence of the specification has a named executable property test, and no request surface ships without enrollment in that roster. A seam review is not enrollment.

binding.reason: there is no request surface to enroll; the roster binds with the first one.

cases.name: output-normalization-is-provably-complete
cases.property: A comparison or recording harness proves its normalization and masking set complete rather than asserting it: two runs of one invocation are byte-equal after masking, so a run-varying field nobody masked fails the harness instead of riding inside a ledgered divergence and inflating its extent. A mask keyed to one serialization form is incomplete by construction — a trace-identifier needle written as compact JSON matches nothing in pretty-printed output. Run-varying fields, trace identifiers and generation timestamps among them, are masked; they are never recorded as divergence.

binding.reason: the corpus audit carries the declared-versus-observed half — every mask and normalization a case declares appears in its recorded bytes, and every one present in the bytes is declared, in both directions and only against names the harness knows — but the two-run byte-equality gate does not exist: the corpus reads recordings and records none, so the gate binds with the first recording or comparison run this line performs.

cases.name: output-parity-cannot-certify-structure
cases.property: Every surface carrying an output-equivalence test also carries at least one structural assertion — statements executed, rows hydrated, bytes read, plan shape — over the same invocation. Output equivalence alone never discharges conformance, because internal shape is what no output comparison can see.

binding.reason: no output comparison runs: every recorded corpus case is dormant behind the activation gate, so there is no invocation for a structural assertion to accompany.

cases.name: scale-assertions-vary-documents-and-bytes-independently
cases.property: A scale assertion varies document count and byte volume independently, and a cost term that moves on the axis its operation does not consume is a failure. A pair whose two profiles differ on both axes at once cannot attribute what moved.

binding.reason: the per-PR flatness pair moves both axes together — its two profiles differ in document count and in body and clutter volume at once — so no assertion isolates an axis today.

cases.name: scoping-wins-are-visible-in-counters
cases.property: A change that narrows the work an operation does is accompanied by a counter that moves. A scoping win masked by surrounding whole-vault work — 1522 documents down to 1, invisible in cost — is not accepted as complete.

binding.reason: no derivation counter exists to move; the rule binds with the first one.

cases.name: steps-report-their-own-outcome
cases.property: A step's verdict is its work's verdict: a downstream reader closing a pipe does not fail a step whose work already succeeded.

binding.reason: no step pipes its output into a reader that can close early — there is no `tee` and no chain carrying a pipeline's earlier failure — so nothing can produce the outcome this forbids; the clause binds with the first step that has one.

cases.name: amortized-periodic-work-stays-amortized
cases.property: Periodic maintenance fires at most once per period and costs a request nothing: the retention sweep runs once a day and adds zero to the request path. Held as a positive control — the shape the rest of the maintenance surface is measured against.

binding.reason: the substrate has no maintenance schedule yet to hold flat.

cases.name: bounded-scoped-resolution-is-the-known-good-shape
cases.property: A resolver bounded by a reverse index and answering by binary-search lookup costs one indexed probe per target and is provably equivalent to the whole-vault fold it replaces. Held as a positive control: the shape a target resolver takes, wherever it is homed.

binding.reason: no resolver exists to hold to the shape.

cases.name: cache-identity-is-total
cases.property: Derived-state identity is a total function of root, schema, build channel and config identity, computed one way at every site. No path opens or upgrades a store outside its identity, no read-only-intent open has a write or wipe effect, and destructive recovery never requires a successful open.

binding.reason: no derived store exists to carry an identity.

cases.name: compiled-work-happens-once-per-generation
cases.property: A pure function of a longer-lived input is computed once per that input's lifetime: compiled matchers once per request rather than once per row, compiled config and predicate field types once per config generation, field-universe knowledge as owner-lifetime state or an indexed lookup. An owner-lifetime resource is acquired once per generation in the same way: no request opens a telemetry file handle of its own, and no request probes owner metadata with a select of its own. Per-row and per-request compile, open and parse counters are zero, and two spellings of one query carry equal derivation counters.

binding.reason: there is no owner generation and no request to compile against.

cases.name: connection-options-are-set-once
cases.property: A socket option is set exactly once per connection, and no live clone of a descriptor exists when its options are altered. Repeated timeout sets on one connection return EINVAL under load, so the second set is the defect rather than the error.

binding.reason: no socket is opened anywhere in the workspace.

cases.name: cost-is-independent-of-vault-size
cases.property: Warm cost and warm counters for reads and for mutations are independent of vault size: the same commands costing 2.5 ms on a 10-document tree and 11.3 to 238.3 ms on a 1593-document one measure vault size, not work. Per-operation cost is a function of the changed set plus its link neighborhood, and a size-independence pair fails the build when an operation's counters track the tree.

binding.reason: the size-independence pair has no request to run; the helper exists and the subject does not.

cases.name: declared-capability-is-exercised
cases.property: Every declared index serves at least one production plan, proven by EXPLAIN over captured SQL, and every substrate reader has at least one production caller. An index that is shipped and populated but serves no query, and a targeted reader whose only callers are its own tests, are failing structural assertions rather than spare capacity.

binding.reason: there is no schema to declare an index and no reader to call.

cases.name: derived-findings-are-materialized-and-maintained
cases.property: Rule-derived findings are stored state: a warm validate reads findings and derives nothing, with a rules-evaluated counter of zero, and a single-document change rewrites finding rows for the affected set alone. Maintaining every finding input while throwing the findings away is the defect.

binding.reason: no findings table exists, and no rule engine derives against one.

cases.name: each-file-is-read-once-per-build
cases.property: A build reads each source file exactly once — the file-read counter for a build equals the file count — and hashing does not buy a second read. Reading every file twice is the shape this forbids: under it read plus parse is 58% of a 565 ms cold build.

binding.reason: nothing builds derived state from a tree yet.

cases.name: encoding-prefix-transparency
cases.property: An encoding prefix is recognized at the extraction seam and never duplicated, relocated or shadowed: a byte-order mark ahead of a frontmatter block leaves the block addressable, no edit synthesizes a second block above the real one, and the prefix bytes are untouched by every edit.

cases.name: freshness-proof-is-off-the-request-path
cases.property: A warm read performs zero filesystem stat operations and loads zero freshness-baseline rows: the freshness counter is zero warm. Trust is asserted by the substrate rather than re-proven per request, where a 1593-row select plus a recursive metadata walk cost ~9.0 ms — 78% of a filtered find and 52% of a warm count. What the mechanism does cost is independent of entries the vault model does not own.

binding.reason: there is no warm read to keep a freshness sweep off.

cases.name: frontmatter-roundtrip-or-refuse
cases.property: Every emitted scalar and key re-parses to exactly the intended value in its actual context — block or flow, value or key position — verified by re-parse rather than by a denylist of shapes. A write not provably round-trip-safe refuses, and no write leaves frontmatter unparseable: an emission judged by a denylist of shapes is the shape this forbids, and under it a flow-sequence item containing a comma becomes two items while one containing a bracket makes every field in the block vanish from every query.

cases.name: harness-condition-waits-have-deadlines
cases.property: A harness wait on a condition carries a deadline the call site declared, over two bounds: the work bound the condition has to become true, and the probe bound one evaluation of it may take. The wait either observes the condition or fails naming the bound it passed and the last state it saw, rather than polling for as long as the run lasts. A slow evaluation is reported as a slow probe rather than as a condition that never held, and neither bound preempts an evaluation already in flight. The deadlines are also sized against each other, not only present: a wait held open across a sequence of other waits carries a budget strictly dominating the sum of the waits it brackets, derived from the budget those waits obey. No nested wait shares a flat constant with a sequence it must outlive — under one shared number the hold expires inside the sequence it was opened to bracket, the subject it parked runs on, and the failure lands wherever that subject went next rather than at the gate.

cases.name: incremental-equals-rebuild
cases.property: For any vault state the incrementally maintained index equals a from-scratch rebuild — after config edits, after alias-table changes, and across path-spelling variants that normalize to one document. Identical input yields byte-identical output, including finding order and offender selection, whatever the cache history: a rebuild that drops 45 findings with no file changed is a divergence, and each derived table carries an explicit invalidation key so a config change re-derives only the tables it keys.

binding.reason: there is no index to maintain incrementally and nothing to rebuild it from.

cases.name: incremental-structures-are-resident-not-rebuilt
cases.property: Blast-radius and resolution structures are maintained substrate state, or are built over the affected set alone. Per-mutation build cost is independent of vault link and file count, and each structure is built at most once per request.

binding.reason: no resolution or reverse-link structure exists.

cases.name: maintenance-touches-the-affected-set-only
cases.property: Maintenance work is O(changed set plus reverse-link blast radius), and every derived table's write scope is that same affected set — no table is exempt. A one-file change that re-walks, re-parses and re-resolves the whole tree is a full build wearing an increment's name, and a wholesale delete of one table's rows while six others are correctly scoped is the same defect in one table.

binding.reason: no increment exists to scope.

cases.name: no-cost-term-multiplies-two-request-varying-quantities
cases.property: No path costs result size times corpus size. Statements per request are O(1) in result-set size — set-valued reads rather than a query per row — a lookup inside an iteration is O(1), and link-impact for N moved documents is N indexed queries rather than a scan of every link. A per-row query loop and a nested scan are failing structural assertions, not slow code.

binding.reason: no reader and no planner exist to exhibit a cost term. A nested scan has occurred outside them — resolving each key of one frontmatter block by scanning that block's parsed mapping — and it is caught by a wall-clock ratio in a soak lane, which is not an evidence kind this stratum binds on; the case binds when a counted or structurally assertable subject exists.

cases.name: one-display-source-per-semantic
cases.property: For a given condition, operator-visible text is a function of the condition alone — identical across direct and routed execution, across CLI and MCP, in every format. Structurally: exactly one Display per error semantic, no call-site literal duplicating a typed error's text, and no debug formatting reachable from user-facing output, with the guard scanning the whole workspace rather than a subtree.

binding.reason: no error type carries prose, and no surface renders one.

cases.name: one-field-edit-is-a-one-field-diff
cases.property: An edit addressed at one field or one section changes exactly those bytes: comments, blank lines, key order, quote style and line terminators outside the span are byte-preserved, and a removal never orphans a continuation line or absorbs a neighbouring field. Section and heading addressing resolves on line boundaries for every accepted heading form, including setext and a heading at end of file with no trailing newline, and the same resolver serves reads and writes.

cases.name: one-membership-predicate-for-the-vault
cases.property: One predicate decides which paths the vault model owns, and one matcher evaluates it. Filtering applies only to entries inside the targeted root, so a dot-prefixed root yields the same document set as a visible one and an implausible root refuses or warns rather than scanning empty; every verb agrees whether a path is addressable; and a refusal names the actual reason — excluded by configuration — never asserting non-existence for a file the tool created.

binding.reason: no walker and no membership configuration exist.

cases.name: one-parser-authority-for-link-text
cases.property: One parser is the authority for link text and target splitting, and the link universe is identical whichever consumer computes it. Code spans are opaque to every targeted parse and rewrite; destination parsing follows URL rules, splitting fragments over the bytes the author wrote and before percent-decoding; a caret is a block sigil only after a hash; and target normalization strips a trailing markdown extension without applying filesystem stem semantics to a version-like name.

binding.reason: the recognition halves are carried today — norn-text's suite holds code opacity, the destination split and the caret rule, and crates/norn-text/tests/markdown_links.rs::the_link_universe_is_the_same_whichever_accessor_computes_it holds one universe across all four accessors. The target-normalization half has no subject at any layer: norn-text normalizes nothing by charter, so the extension-stripping rule binds wherever resolution lands and this case stays dormant until it does.

cases.name: one-path-equivalence-policy
cases.property: One path-equivalence relation applies identically at every comparison site, and the filesystem-case policy is stated once. Selection and verification never fold case asymmetrically, subtree and collision checks use the same relation as the move they gate, and a deduplicated survivor carries the spelling the directory entry has.

binding.reason: no path comparison site exists.

cases.name: one-resolver-for-document-identity
cases.property: One resolver answers every target string, and every verb resolves a given string to the same candidate set. A candidate set whose size is not one refuses, naming the candidates; a path qualifier filters candidates rather than being discarded or compared against bare stems; and a plan is built from the resolved path, never from the raw argument.

binding.reason: no resolver exists, and no verb has a target to resolve.

cases.name: parse-failure-is-not-absence
cases.property: A parse failure is a distinct, propagated state and is never collapsed into absence. Every consumer surfaces the diagnostic before treating fields as missing, an unparseable document is never silently dropped from a query result, and no two mutation arms disagree about whether one document is legible.

binding.reason: diagnostics are produced; no consumer exists to hold to not-dropping them. Carve-out: a frontmatter tag string the grammar does not describe yields no tag AND no diagnostic, by ruling — judging such a string is validation's venue, so its silence is a decision rather than a collapsed failure.

cases.name: present-but-unusable-config-refuses-loudly
cases.property: Absence and unreadability are distinct outcomes: a configuration that is present but unusable refuses with a specific diagnostic rather than falling back to defaults. No configuration path blocks unboundedly, panics, or wraps on overflow; an unreadable parent directory is an error rather than an absence; a parsed version field is read or does not exist; and configuration diagnostics are deterministic and complete, naming every offender in a stable order.

binding.reason: there is no configuration file to load.

cases.name: projections-are-what-the-answer-needs
cases.property: Every projected column and every optional facet has a consumer on the path that requests it, and projections derive from the requested output shape. Peak resident set and wire bytes for a body-less verb are independent of vault body bytes: 15.1 MB of head and body text loaded for an engine that reads neither, and 419 KB on the wire for ten documents, are the same defect at two boundaries.

binding.reason: no reader projects columns and no wire report carries them.

cases.name: recovery-is-never-billed-to-the-next-caller
cases.property: Request latency after an out-of-band change is within a constant factor of warm, and recovery runs off the request thread: a 30-byte edit turning a 9.27 ms read into 356.13 ms is recovery billed to a blocked reader. Connection establishment is likewise outside request service — a request's connection-open counter is zero — and a counter proves zero derivation inside the request.

binding.reason: there is no warm state to recover and no pool to grow.

cases.name: relative-time-and-locale-resolve-against-a-declared-basis
cases.property: A relative date word resolves against a declared time zone rather than against whichever basis its call site reached for: `today` names the same day boundary in a filter, in a default and in a rendered field, and the zone it resolved in is stated wherever the word is accepted. The locale governing collation and case folding is chosen by a stated precedence over its inputs, so two surfaces reading one environment order and fold identically.

binding.reason: no date-word resolver and no locale-sensitive comparison exists to declare a basis for.

cases.name: statements-are-prepared-once
cases.property: Prepared statements are cached per connection, and the compilation counter per request is a bounded constant independent of row count. A per-document loader is the shape this forbids: it compiles ~12,700 statements per mutation, and statement compilation is ~32 ms of a 139 ms insert phase.

binding.reason: no connection prepares a statement.

cases.name: storage-configuration-is-explicit
cases.property: Every durability and performance pragma is set explicitly and asserted, rather than inherited as a default, and statistics collection runs on a declared schedule rather than on every build.

binding.reason: no database is opened to configure.

cases.name: substrate-capabilities-are-probed-before-they-are-relied-on
cases.property: A substrate capability the system leans on is proven at corpus scale before it carries load: a JSON aggregation that reports malformed input for valid, self-written JSON is found by a probe over generated trees, or the capability is not used and the alternative is a declared design choice.

binding.reason: no substrate capability is relied on yet.

cases.name: targeted-lookups-are-indexed
cases.property: A question about one identifier is one indexed statement, and statements executed are O(1) and independent of vault size. This binds every re-entry point: resolving one string to one path, asking which documents link here, checking membership for k paths as k probes rather than a materialized map, and every advisory uniqueness or collision check — an advisory never introduces a whole-vault term.

binding.reason: no index and no targeted reader exist.

cases.name: text-search-is-indexed
cases.property: Full-text search executes against a text index, and its cost scales with match count rather than with corpus bytes. A case-folded substring scan over every body is not a search implementation.

binding.reason: there is no text index and no search surface.

cases.name: unsatisfiable-config-is-rejected-at-load
cases.property: A configuration that cannot be satisfied is rejected at load, naming every contributing rule, rather than surfacing per write as a refusal listing no permitted value. Every rule-selection site reads one shared effective matcher — no site reads a raw path pattern, so a rule constrained only by its target is never treated as applying to every document — a configured repair never writes a value the validator immediately flags, and rule names used as selectors are unique.

binding.reason: there is no rule vocabulary to check for satisfiability.

cases.name: warm-state-survives-process-lifetime
cases.property: Substrate state survives process lifetime by construction, and the ratio of a cold ephemeral start to a warm one is a declared bounded number: 565 ms against 17 ms is a state store born and destroyed with its process.

binding.reason: no persistent derived state exists.

cases.name: audit-stream-integrity
cases.property: Every filesystem effect appears in the plan, in the forecast, and in the audit stream; audit records survive failure paths; every mutation on every surface lands in a real sink rather than a discard; trace ids are real or absent, never fabricated from a seeded generator; and every log line is time-correlatable.

binding.reason: no audit stream and no applier exist.

cases.name: barriers-fail-closed
cases.property: A barrier fails closed. A change to one is tested in the direction that would let something through, not only in the direction that would refuse too much: trading a spurious refusal for a silent miss trades a safe failure for a dangerous one.

binding.reason: no barrier exists to fail either way.

cases.name: cache-entries-are-owned-and-reclaimed
cases.property: A derived-state entry is owned by its creator and reclaimed with it; maintenance never runs on the request path; eviction re-validates its classification under the same lock it deletes with; and harness traffic is isolated by construction. An ambient sweep or a long derivation emits a liveness signal past a duration or count threshold, so 75 seconds of silence behind a backlog is a failure rather than a wait. Entries nobody reclaims and a prune billed to a request are the shapes this forbids: they reach 61,103 entries and 8.0 GB, and they block one command for over two minutes.

binding.reason: nothing creates a derived-state entry to own.

cases.name: degradation-is-reported-with-a-direction-correct-remedy
cases.property: Any fallback that drops a headline guarantee emits an operator-visible signal on the caller's channel at the moment it engages, with an actionable remedy that points at the component actually at fault. No state computed for the operator is discarded, and silent degradation is not a state the system can be in — silence is the defect under test.

binding.reason: there is no routed path that could degrade.

cases.name: finding-payload-is-bounded
cases.property: Finding payload grows at most linearly with vault size at fixed defect density, and per-finding candidate lists are bounded by a cap with a total alongside. No ambiguity class yields payload quadratic in its own size: 55 KB becoming 8.4 MB across three times the documents is the shape this forbids.

binding.reason: no finding is produced or serialized.

cases.name: owner-inputs-are-identity-or-re-read
cases.property: Every owner input is part of the owner's identity or is re-read per request; nothing is resolved once at summon and consulted forever. A configuration or registration change is visible to the next request, and a configuration snapshot is one read — the bytes parsed are the bytes fingerprinted.

binding.reason: there is no owner to summon.

cases.name: per-file-atomicity-and-durability
cases.property: Every file written goes through temp, rename, fsync of the file and fsync of the parent, and every document-mutating path routes through that one primitive. An interrupted run leaves each document fully old or fully new with no orphaned temp; a cross-device placement fails closed rather than falling back to copy-then-unlink; and destructive ordering is gated, so no redirect is committed before the removal it redirects away from.

binding.reason: the write primitive exists and carries two of this case's clauses — shadow, rename, fsync of the file and fsync of the parent, and a cross-device placement that refuses rather than copying. The rest have no subject: an interrupted run needs process-kill injection, no orphaned staging file needs the sweep that clears one, and there is no document-mutating path to route or destructive ordering to gate. A binding names tests for the whole property, so this stays dormant until those land.

cases.name: plan-level-atomicity-and-truthful-partial-reporting
cases.property: The whole plan validates before the first write — containment, collision, preconditions, every pass — and two operations targeting one path are rejected. On failure a machine-readable per-operation report persists, naming what committed and what remains, including every unmoved or skipped file by name; shared report fields accumulate across passes rather than being overwritten by a later one; recovery is a regenerable plan; and no declared plan field goes unread by the applier.

binding.reason: no plan vocabulary and no applier exist.

cases.name: poisoned-state-self-heals-and-writes-are-never-ambiguous
cases.property: Initial creation of derived state is exclusive, and any poisoned handle — missing database, descriptor exhaustion, corruption, a recovered lock still refusing — is detected and rebuilt without operator intervention. Every write resolves to applied or not applied: never may-have-applied, never landing after the client's verdict. The client learns within bounded time which of the two it was, and a legitimate long rebuild is distinguishable from an indefinite hang rather than presenting as one. A liveness verdict derives from observed progress and is never issued for a request the server completed.

binding.reason: no resident process holds state that could be poisoned.

cases.name: preconditions-come-from-plan-time
cases.property: Preconditions are captured at plan or forecast time and never re-derived at apply, so a hash hydrated from apply-time state is tautological. What the operator confirmed is what applies, or the operation refuses; a confirmation is accepted only against a still-valid anchor the caller observed; and precondition comparison uses the query layer's typing rules rather than its own coercion.

binding.reason: no planner captures a precondition.

cases.name: read-that-feeds-a-write-is-under-the-writes-lock
cases.property: Every read feeding a write occurs inside the write's exclusive scope, enforced structurally at one seam rather than by convention repeated per handler. Final placement is exclusive-create unless force is given, so a concurrent external create is never clobbered, and a new mutation cannot opt out of the seam.

binding.reason: no mutation handler and no lock seam exist.

cases.name: reads-are-not-blocked-by-writes
cases.property: A read's wait is bounded and reported, and an in-flight write does not serialize the read surface. One session mutex held across a blocking round trip is the shape this forbids: under it a 40-second apply blocks every concurrent read for 40 seconds with no diagnostic.

binding.reason: there is no serving surface on which reads and writes could contend.

cases.name: vault-root-containment
cases.property: Every operation target's parent canonicalizes under the canonical vault root, checked once in the shared apply layer, with the check-to-write window closed by handle pinning. A lexical guard is not containment: parent traversal, absolute paths and a symlinked directory inside the vault each escape one.

binding.reason: no apply layer exists to contain.

cases.name: warm-requests-derive-nothing
cases.property: A warm request derives nothing: every derivation counter reads zero. Counters are zero for every substrate input the handler does not read, so a verb that reads no vault state costs the round-trip floor and nothing more — a whole-tree stat sweep billed to a verb whose closure ignores the vault is ~9.0 ms of pure tax.

binding.reason: there is no warm request to count.

cases.name: a-limit-bounds-hydration-through-one-paging-seam
cases.property: Ordering and paging are expressed once, in SQL, and every verb offering them routes through that seam. Rows hydrated are at most the page size whatever the filter shape: a path glob never voids a limit, and no verb re-implements sort and page in memory after full hydration.

binding.reason: no read builder emits SQL and no verb pages.

cases.name: cache-is-authoritative-for-content
cases.property: Where the substrate stores content, request paths read it from the substrate: the warm filesystem-read counter for a read verb is zero. A passing test pinning that stored text reproduces a file byte for byte is an invariant the read path uses, not a fact it ignores.

binding.reason: no substrate stores document content.

cases.name: comparison-semantics-are-one-rule
cases.property: One comparison semantics governs every engine: SQL-bound and in-process comparison agree on every case, including numeric-versus-text equality, pinned by explicit tests. Matching is symmetric in the shape of the stored value, so a bracket-wrapped and a plain spelling of one value compare alike in both directions, and date filters are chronologically correct regardless of offset — or the lexical contract is explicit and signalled on mixed-offset input.

binding.reason: no query layer compares values.

cases.name: existence-probes-and-per-request-allocation-are-bounded
cases.property: An existence check executes a select-one-shaped statement, and does-any-error-exist is one existence query rather than a scan. Within one request each target is resolved at most once and each document loaded at most once, and per-request allocation of derived collections is bounded by response size rather than by corpus size.

binding.reason: no read verb probes for existence.

cases.name: machine-formats-carry-completeness-in-band
cases.property: Every machine format carries an in-band completeness signal, so a consumer reading stdout alone knows whether the set was truncated. An echoed offset round-trips exactly: the next page begins at the successor of the last record returned, with no gap and no overlap.

binding.reason: no machine format is emitted.

cases.name: narrowing-arguments-narrow-work
cases.property: A narrowing argument on any verb narrows the work, not just the output: scoped counters are strictly below unscoped ones, and a narrowing predicate never increases cost. Filtering after evaluating every document — validate over one path costing what the whole tree costs, repair evaluating 1593 documents then filtering to the requested paths — is the shape this forbids.

binding.reason: no verb accepts a narrowing argument.

cases.name: no-in-memory-query-layer
cases.property: Each read verb's answer is produced by SQL. Any in-memory post-pass over more rows than the verb returns is a declared exception carrying a counter ceiling, and rows materialized are at most rows returned times a constant.

binding.reason: there is no read surface to answer.

cases.name: predicate-filtering-in-sql-is-the-known-good-shape
cases.property: A verb's core predicate compiles to a SQL where-clause the database answers, with rows hydrated equal to rows returned. Held as a positive control: the read shape every other read verb is measured against.

binding.reason: no read builder exists to hold to the shape.

cases.name: set-valued-answers-are-pushed-down
cases.property: Cardinality, grouping and distinct-value answers execute as aggregate SQL with zero document rows hydrated, and their cost is a function of the number of distinct groups rather than of body bytes. Counting by hydrating every match and taking the length, and folding folder names out of fully hydrated documents, are the same defect.

binding.reason: no aggregate read surface exists.

cases.name: unknown-sort-or-projection-keys-never-silently-no-op
cases.property: The field universe is exact — schema keys united with observed keys — and the diagnostic is a biconditional: a request component is reported unsatisfiable exactly when it is unsatisfiable. An unknown sort, column or predicate key never silently degrades a result, a malformed glob is never swallowed into a zero-match answer, a path filter that cannot match by construction — a bare directory where the grammar matches globs — is reported rather than answered with a silent empty set, and a missing named section is a distinguishable miss rather than a silent whole-document substitution. The diagnostic reaches every surface, and the exit code distinguishes not-fully-satisfiable from satisfiable-with-zero-matches, which stays success.

binding.reason: no query surface parses a sort or projection key.

cases.name: cascade-preserves-link-syntax
cases.property: A rewritten link preserves every syntactic component except the target — embed marker, alias, anchor, block reference. Rewriting is occurrence-addressed rather than first-match, and only unambiguously resolving occurrences are rewritten; the rest are skipped and named. A raw prefix strip is the shape this forbids: one prefix miss turns a transclusion with an alias into a plain link while the report claims three backlinks rewritten.

binding.reason: no cascade rewriter exists.

cases.name: created-documents-are-mutable
cases.property: Every document the system can produce it can subsequently address and mutate. Empty or null frontmatter promotes to an empty mapping, an absent block is synthesized, and a present-but-empty key is a valid target; refusal is reserved for frontmatter that genuinely is not a mapping.

binding.reason: no creation verb and no field editor exist.

cases.name: error-variant-matches-the-operation-reported
cases.property: Every failure carries a code drawn from the semantic domain of the operation actually attempted, and the code's fault class agrees with the exit code. Falsifiable as a total table: operation kind crossed with injected failure point maps to a code, asserted exhaustively under fault injection, with no code from another operation's domain reachable and no internal-error code reachable from any user-controlled input.

binding.reason: no operation exists to fail, and no error taxonomy to draw a code from.

cases.name: forecast-and-apply-are-one-classifier
cases.property: Forecast and apply are one classifier over the same bytes. What apply touches is a subset of what the forecast reported, and under no concurrent drift the two are equal set-wise and count-wise, including skips with their reasons. Every occurrence is classified individually rather than by first raw match; an unresolved or ambiguous match is never rewritten silently, but refused or reported under the same classification apply will use; and a forecast is labelled a forecast in every format.

binding.reason: there is no planner and no applier to compare; the generator emits ambiguous-stem and dangling-link trees, and nothing yet consumes them.

cases.name: format-never-implies-consent
cases.property: Output format is a presentation choice with zero consent semantics. Writing requires explicit confirmation on every verb, uniformly, so asking for structured output never applies a plan.

binding.reason: no verb writes, and no format flag exists.

cases.name: integrity-fingerprints-are-scoped-and-computed-once
cases.property: Integrity verification for a mutation is O(affected set) and is computed at most once per commit. A whole-tree fingerprint recomputed twice per confirmed mutation measures the vault, not the change.

binding.reason: no commit computes a fingerprint.

cases.name: mutation-honors-its-planned-flags
cases.property: The applier's filesystem effect set is exactly the plan's declared effect set. No directory, file or temp survives that the plan did not declare and the forecast did not report; a move with parents disabled onto a missing parent refuses and leaves the directory set unchanged; a dry run of any verb leaves the tree unchanged, inode and mtime included; and one deterministic missing-parent policy governs every creation call site, so no site creates ahead of the applier.

binding.reason: no plan type and no applier exist; the pre-and-post directory-and-inode assertion has nothing to run against.

cases.name: one-snapshot-per-request
cases.property: A request acquires exactly one substrate snapshot — the snapshot counter reads one — and the commit consumes the same snapshot the verb read. Two independent snapshots inside one confirmed mutation cost ~110 ms of a 182.9 ms operation.

binding.reason: nothing acquires a snapshot.

cases.name: one-verdict-and-one-coercion-basis-per-post-state
cases.property: One constraint engine answers for the intended post-state: for a given configuration, document and intended post-state, every write path returns the same verdict, and reported warnings equal the validator's finding set for that post-state. Every type and coercion decision resolves against the post-state's applicable rules, not the outgoing state's, so one atomic call that changes a document's type coerces its other fields under the incoming type.

binding.reason: there is no constraint engine and no write path to hold to one verdict; the write path is the last engine this property needs, which is why it binds a layer below the element-versus-collection rule.

cases.name: resolved-path-gates-resolved-path-reports
cases.property: Every path gate applies to the resolved path and is re-checked after resolution, so a pattern constraining a resolved filename is never evaluated against an unresolved template. Every operation's report and audit span names that operation's own resolved target.

binding.reason: no path template is resolved and no gate reads one.

cases.name: whole-vault-work-is-declared-and-triggered-deliberately
cases.property: Vault-wide work happens only where it is declared, and the declared set is a fixed enumerable roster asserted by test; row-touch counters on undeclared paths are bounded by the declared affected set. Full derivation is reached only at cold start, integrity failure, or a scheduled health scan — never from the request path, and never under the mutation lock — and precondition evaluation is one indexed statement per selector.

binding.reason: there is no roster to declare and no request path to keep clear.

cases.name: write-through-the-composed-post-state
cases.property: A mutation's commit consumes the bytes and parsed post-state the mutation composed: filesystem reads per touched file within a mutation request are zero, and content hashes are computed at most once. Re-reading what the mutation just composed is the shape this forbids: it costs one single-field write three reads and three hashes of its own changed file.

binding.reason: nothing composes a post-state to write through.

cases.name: write-verification-gate-covers-the-whole-contract
cases.property: The verification gate's coverage equals the contract's promises: where the contract preserves comments, ordering and terminators, the gate compares those bytes rather than a semantic projection of them. Every splice is re-parsed and confirmed before commit rather than trusted on a scanner's proposed span, and the gate's adequacy is itself tested by mutating it and requiring the suite to go red.

binding.reason: no write path exists to gate.

cases.name: element-vs-collection-semantics-are-one-rule
cases.property: One element-versus-collection semantics is shared by query, validate, mutate and repair. A value a write path accepts is never flagged by the validator; a finding a repair rule targets is always matchable by its compare-and-swap precondition; element-wise operations compare against elements rather than against a wrapped whole; and findings converge to one per path, field and value against the intersection of applicable constraints rather than one per co-applying rule.

binding.reason: no validator, mutator or repair planner exists to agree; the repair planner's compare-and-swap precondition is the last engine this property needs, which is why it binds a layer above the one-verdict rule.

cases.name: link-repair-targets-unresolvable-text
cases.property: Link repair can target text that does not resolve — that is the case repair exists for — and repair guidance is not gated on membership of the validation scope, so a document outside that scope still receives it.

binding.reason: no repair planner exists.

cases.name: argv-accepts-leading-hyphen-content
cases.property: A flag taking free text accepts a value beginning with a hyphen, and a refusal never points at an escape convention that does not apply to the invocation refused.

binding.reason: there is no argv grammar.

cases.name: cross-surface-capability-parity
cases.property: One parameter and report vocabulary serves every surface: any invocation expressible on one surface is expressible on the other with identical results, diagnostics and refusals, and one envelope convention covers every command. Guards live at the engine rather than in a renderer, and parity is enforced by a generated gate over parameters and payload shapes rather than by hand-kept twins.

binding.reason: there is one surface at most and no vocabulary to render twice.

cases.name: distinct-values-render-distinguishably
cases.property: Values that differ render differently: an empty string, an empty collection and an absent value are distinguishable in every rendering, key column included.

binding.reason: there is no render seam.

cases.name: every-accepted-flag-has-an-observable-effect
cases.property: Every surfaced flag is structurally required to reach a behavior seam, or it is rejected: a flag that parses and plumbs nowhere is impossible rather than merely absent. An escape-hatch flag zeroes the counter of the work it claims to skip; explicit-versus-explicit conflicts refuse; last-operation-wins is uniform wherever override is the semantics; a shared guardrail flag behaves identically across sibling verbs; no grammar shape can panic; and help prose and grammar agree by generation.

binding.reason: there is no grammar and no behavior seam for a flag to reach.

cases.name: every-warning-reaches-every-surface
cases.property: One warnings vocabulary, one empty policy and one truncation policy across every verb, and every warning and skip is reachable from every surface with its reason and its subject named — including which link was left stale and which element of a collection was bad. Each warning names the actual mismatch, and no message duplicates the prefix its parser already emitted.

binding.reason: no verb produces a warning and no surface renders one.

cases.name: exit-code-is-a-total-function-of-outcome-class
cases.property: The exit code derives from the outcome class alone. A refusal that wrote nothing never shares a code with a partial apply, no code depends on which parser caught the input, and one logical failure class carries one code regardless of the path that produced it.

binding.reason: the binary has no outcomes to classify.

cases.name: failure-is-carried-in-the-protocols-native-channel
cases.property: An outcome is carried in the protocol's native failure channel on every surface, so a completed apply, a preflight refusal and a partial-apply failure are distinguishable without parsing an in-band report. The same condition yields the same machine code and envelope everywhere, asserted across surfaces, and a machine code is never laundered into prose on the way out.

binding.reason: no protocol surface exists to carry a failure.

cases.name: help-states-the-contract-nothing-else
cases.property: User-facing help states the present-tense contract only: no provenance, no internal notes, no task identifiers, no flags that do not exist. Documented interfaces are generated from or asserted against the live grammar and tool catalog in both directions, so a functional flag missing from its command's help fails as loudly as a documented flag missing from the grammar. An argument form the grammar refuses is stated in the help of the argument that refuses it, and an argument rejected for its form is reported as rejected rather than left unaddressable: a heading operation that refuses a `#`-prefixed heading while its help says nothing about hashes leaves a real heading with no spelling that reaches it.

binding.reason: there is no help surface and no grammar to generate it from.

cases.name: one-spelling-per-identity-everywhere
cases.property: One identity has one spelling on every surface. The product name is identical across help, version, errors and completions and is reported as itself by every protocol handshake; a skip reason or operation code has one casing form wherever it appears — serialized field, accessor, flag value, map key.

binding.reason: the binary has no name-bearing surfaces and no operation codes.

cases.name: per-invocation-identity-cost-is-bounded
cases.property: Per-invocation identity cost is independent of configuration size: identity is established without reading and hashing the configuration body on a warm path.

binding.reason: no client establishes an identity.

cases.name: rendering-survives-the-terminal-it-lands-in
cases.property: Meaningful emphasis never depends on a faint attribute alone, which renders as the default colour on common terminals, and table shape does not depend on the terminal declining to soft-wrap a long cell. Styling comes from one render seam every verb goes through, so no verb renders plain where its siblings render styled, and the decision to style at all is a function of the stream rather than of which verb wrote to it.

binding.reason: there is no render seam and nothing writes to a terminal.

cases.name: suite-references-move-with-the-suite
cases.property: A suite's reference moves with the suite: an installed binary ahead of a pinned reference reports skew rather than turning the suite red.

binding.reason: no suite runs against an installed binary: the `norn` binary is a stub with no version to pin a reference to. The first suite that compares against one is the subject.
